Jobs · the build against the drawing

Stream HH, 2026-09-04. Every locked frame beside its build, for the owner's verdict. The drawings are 01-the-jobs-screens.html and 02-the-jobs-settings.html, locked 2026-09-04; the build is the module at jobs/ui, commit a986a59.

Method. One browser — the machine's own Chrome 152, headless — at one width, 1280 px, both sides served from one origin. Each locked frame is served standalone, its own markup and its own stylesheet, so nothing renders the drawing differently from the build. The build is photographed through its capture harness, which fakes the host and nothing else: the identity, the granted capabilities, the property (Asia/Qatar, en-GB) and the answers to host.call are the harness's; the module's code, stylesheet and token references are the shipped ones, and the tokens injected are the fourteen the shell publishes and no more.

Fidelity is measured, not eyed — the standing rule since the overlay's rejection. The drawings' values are read out of their own CSS and the build's out of its computed styles, in the same browser, and compared as numbers. Section B is that comparison.

VerdictCountWhat it means
built60on the screen, as drawn

Total elements78across 26 frames and the cross-cutting six

Capture limits, plainly. Three states needed a stub and are marked no message answers this rather than built: who is on shift and who holds a headship (no Workforce or Identity client exists in the application SDK, so the seam returns empty on a property and the recorded example stands in), and a schedule's recurrence (the plan lives in the Engineering app on the platform scheduler; TEMPORAL-Q1 settles it and this surface designs against Temporal Schedules when II's round lands). A synthetic scroll could not reach past the first page of a department's people on the Live tab, so those cards are photographed at their first six of nine and fourteen — the state a person sees before scrolling, which is the state the frame draws. Frames 01-8 and 02-11 have no build pane by their own captions: one is a pointer to the second page, the other is the resolution rule drawn as a table rather than a screen.

A · the two the audit caught

These are the argument for the method: both were invisible to a suite that asserts content, and both were caught by putting the photograph beside the drawing. The before is the build at c557b22, checked out and photographed for this page; the after is the build now.

The timer counted from the machine's clock

The frame draws 00:23:41. The build subtracted the session's start from new Date(), so on the capture machine it read 42:16:53 and climbing. On a property the same error is silent — a desktop whose clock has drifted shows a figure the hotel never had, on the one number a supervisor uses to judge a promise. The service already computes worked time against the clock the property runs on, so it now sends the figure (JobView.running_seconds) and the module renders it; the module's own subtraction is deleted, not corrected.

before · the build at c557b22
after · the build now

The work controls appeared for somebody who does not hold the job

With only job.read granted, the build drew Pause and Stop. The reasoning was right — accept, start, pause and stop are the assignee's own acts and no permission gates them — and the implementation was wrong, because the module cannot tell who is looking: ModuleIdentity carries capabilities, not a user. Pressing one would have been refused by the service, which is a control that lies. viewer_is_assignee is now computed where the caller is established, and that viewer gets no action row at all.

before · only job.read granted
after · only job.read granted

B · what differs everywhere, measured

Read out of the two pages' own CSS and the module's computed styles in the same browser, not judged by eye. Identical where it matters to the eye and to the hand: head height 56px, head padding 22px, tab 13px with 19px above, column head 11px uppercase at 0.88px tracking, cell padding 10px, pill radius 999px at 11px/600 with 9px sides, job number 12px ui-monospace.

The palettediverged · ruledMeasured, not eyed: the drawing names its own hexes in its :root; the build is painted by the fourteen tokens the shell publishes. brand #6b7cff → #818cf8, bad #ff5c7a → #f87171, ok #3ecf8e → #34d399, warn #f5b53f → #fbbf24, line .09 → .07, ink #e9ecf5 → #e8ebf4. ADR 0106 and the drawing's own first rule: the tokens are the authority and the drawing's hexes were an approximation of them.
The window framediverged · ruledThe drawing puts the app in a floating card — 14px radius, 1px border, glass fill — because it is drawn inside a page. The build fills its realm: no border, no radius, --color-surface. In production the module is the window and the shell owns the frame. Measured: radius 14px → 0px, border 1px → 0px.
The panel radiusdiverged · ruledCard radius 12px in the drawing, 16px in the build — --radius-panel: 1rem, one of the fourteen. The token wins over the drawn value by the same rule.
The date formdiverged · ruled02 Sep 13:31 drawn, 02 Sept, 13:31 built under en-GB, Sep 02, 01:31 PM under en-US. JOBS-Q1(8) working: the form is the property's, from locale and timezone, and no package writes its own.
The body typediverged · openMeasured: 14px Inter drawn, 13.5px on the shell's --font-sans built. The family is ruled — Inter does not reach a module realm. The size is not: 13.5px is the chrome Workforce set and this module copied, and the drawing said 14px. One of the two should give.
Composed prose still carries datesdiverged · openThe service sends finished sentences for some values — “Due at · 02 Sep 14:10 · policy P1 = 40 min”, “Accepted · 02 Sep 13:47”, the Live tab's “last nudge”. Their date form does not follow the viewer's property the way every other timestamp now does. Fixing it means sending the instants beside the prose, as the job header already does. Queued for this redline.
